summary: An investigation by The Atlantic reported allegations from several men who said Bryan Singer sexually abused them when they were teenagers. Singer called the report a homophobic smear and denied the claims.

title: Oxford grooming gang members handed life sentences
summary: Further members of an Oxford grooming gang received life sentences for raping and abusing a schoolgirl.

title: John Engler resigns as Michigan State interim president
summary: Engler resigned under pressure after comments about Nassar survivors drew widespread condemnation.

title: Kevin Spacey charged with indecent assault in Nantucket case
summary: Massachusetts prosecutors charged Kevin Spacey with felony indecent assault and battery over a 2016 encounter with an 18-year-old at a Nantucket bar. Spacey denied the charge.

title: State Medical Board confirms it holds complaint records on Strauss
summary: The State Medical Board of Ohio confirmed it had records of complaints about Strauss from its 1996 investigation, which never led to discipline.

title: CBS denies Les Moonves $120 million severance after board investigation
summary: The CBS board concluded after an outside investigation that it had grounds to fire Les Moonves for cause, including willful failure to cooperate, and denied him a $120 million severance package.

title: Cardinal Pell found guilty of historical sexual offences
summary: A Melbourne jury convicted Pell of offences against two choirboys in the 1990s; the verdict was suppressed from publication in Australia until February 2019.

title: Pope removes Pell and another cardinal from his advisory council
summary: Pope Francis dropped two cardinals linked to abuse cases, including Pell, from his Council of Cardinals.

title: Police found trove of nude images in Tyndall's storage unit, sources say
summary: Investigators reportedly recovered large numbers of images of women from a storage unit tied to Tyndall early in the LAPD probe.

title: USA Gymnastics files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: USA Gymnastics filed for bankruptcy protection in Indianapolis, pausing hundreds of lawsuits from Nassar survivors and the USOC decertification process.

title: Grand jury convened to hear evidence against ex-USC gynecologist
summary: Los Angeles County prosecutors convened a criminal grand jury to hear evidence about Tyndall's alleged abuse of patients.

title: Miami Herald series reexamines Epstein's secret 2008 deal and the victims it left behind
summary: The Miami Herald's Perversion of Justice series, with a timeline of the case, detailed how federal prosecutors led by Alexander Acosta negotiated a lenient deal with Epstein and kept victims in the dark.

title: Former MSU President Lou Anna Simon charged with lying to police
summary: Simon was charged with lying to state police investigators about what she knew of a 2014 complaint against Nassar. She denied wrongdoing.

title: Accusers say more than 20 Ohio State staff knew of Strauss concerns
summary: Plaintiffs alleged in court filings that more than 20 university employees were aware of concerns about Strauss.

title: U.S. Olympic Committee moves to revoke USA Gymnastics' governing status
summary: The USOC began proceedings to decertify USA Gymnastics as the sport's national governing body over its handling of the Nassar crisis.

title: Ireland decides to exhume remains at Tuam mass grave
summary: The Irish government approved a forensic excavation of the Tuam site so children's remains could be identified and reburied.

title: USC agrees to tentative $215 million class-action settlement with Tyndall patients
summary: USC announced a proposed $215 million federal class-action settlement covering former patients of Tyndall, with tiered payments and campus reforms.

title: More than 250 women file state-court suits against USC, rejecting class deal
summary: Attorneys for more than 250 former Tyndall patients filed lawsuits in state court and criticized the proposed federal settlement.

title: Justice Department opens federal investigation into clergy abuse in Pennsylvania dioceses
summary: Federal prosecutors in Pennsylvania served subpoenas on Catholic dioceses across the state, opening the first known federal investigation into clergy sexual abuse and its concealment in the wake of the grand jury report.

title: Former USA Gymnastics CEO Steve Penny arrested on evidence tampering charge
summary: Penny was arrested on a Texas indictment accusing him of removing documents from the Karolyi Ranch related to the Nassar investigation.

title: Pope defrocks two retired Chilean bishops over abuse
summary: Francis laicized two retired Chilean bishops accused of abusing minors, a rare sanction against bishops.

title: Prosecutors drop one count in Weinstein criminal case
summary: A judge dismissed one sexual assault count at prosecutors' request after questions arose about the investigation, while the remaining charges stood.

title: Vatican defrocks Chilean priest Fernando Karadima
summary: Pope Francis expelled Karadima from the priesthood, years after a church tribunal found he had abused minors.

title: Fox settles remaining claims in Scottie Nell Hughes retaliation suit
summary: Hughes settled her remaining retaliation claims with Fox for an undisclosed amount after a judge earlier dismissed her assault claim and other counts.

title: German bishops' MHG study documents thousands of abuse cases
summary: A church-commissioned study found 3,677 children were abused by 1,670 clergy between 1946 and 2014 and that records had been destroyed or manipulated.

title: Cosby sentenced to 3 to 10 years in state prison, labeled sexually violent predator
summary: A Montgomery County judge sentenced Cosby to three to 10 years in state prison and designated him a sexually violent predator; he was taken into custody immediately.

title: Pope summons world's bishops to summit on clerical abuse
summary: Francis called the presidents of all bishops' conferences to Rome for a February 2019 meeting on protecting minors.

title: New allegations against Les Moonves emerge in second New Yorker report
summary: A follow-up report detailed accounts from six additional women accusing Les Moonves of sexual misconduct, as CBS negotiated his exit.

title: Les Moonves resigns as CBS chairman and CEO
summary: Les Moonves stepped down from CBS hours after new allegations were published; CBS and Moonves pledged $20 million to groups supporting the #MeToo movement, deducted from any severance.

title: Judge denies Nassar's request for a new sentencing hearing
summary: An Eaton County judge rejected Nassar's bid for resentencing and a new judge, which argued his sentences were tainted by bias.

title: USC restructures student health center in wake of Tyndall scandal
summary: USC leaders described staffing and oversight changes at the Engemann Student Health Center aimed at rebuilding student trust.

title: Tyndall's medical license suspended pending state medical board decision
summary: Tyndall was barred from practicing medicine while the Medical Board of California weighed a final decision on his license.

title: Pope Francis visits Ireland amid anger over clergy abuse
summary: Francis traveled to Ireland for the World Meeting of Families as survivors and politicians pressed him on decades of abuse and cover-up.

title: Federal civil rights office opens review of Ohio State's Strauss response
summary: The U.S. Education Department's Office for Civil Rights opened an investigation into how Ohio State handled complaints about Strauss under Title IX.

title: Olympians Kyla Ross and Madison Kocian say Nassar abused them
summary: Two members of U.S. Olympic teams said publicly that they were also among Nassar's victims.

title: Pennsylvania grand jury report says more than 300 priests abused over 1,000 children in six dioceses
summary: A statewide grand jury report released by the Pennsylvania attorney general identified more than 300 accused priests and over 1,000 child victims across six dioceses over seven decades. It concluded that church leaders systematically covered up the abuse.

title: Inquiry finds 'appalling' abuse at Ampleforth and Downside schools
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry's report on two Benedictine boarding schools found monks and staff abused pupils over decades and that the institutions prioritised reputations over children.

title: IICSA report damns culture of acceptance of abuse at Ampleforth and Downside
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (IICSA)
summary: The inquiry found the Benedictine schools prioritized monks and reputation over pupils, allowing abusers to continue for decades.

title: Nikias formally steps down; Wanda Austin becomes interim USC president
summary: Nikias left the presidency earlier than planned after calls to hasten his departure, with trustee Wanda Austin named interim president.

title: Texts show former Ohio State coach urged Jordan accusers to recant
summary: NBC News reported text messages in which former head wrestling coach Russ Hellickson urged former wrestlers to retract statements about Jordan.

title: Ten more former students sue Ohio State over Strauss
summary: Ten additional former students filed suit alleging Ohio State failed to stop abuse by Strauss.

title: New Yorker reports misconduct allegations against CBS chief Les Moonves
summary: A Ronan Farrow investigation reported that six women accused CBS chief executive Les Moonves of sexual harassment or intimidation and described a wider culture of misconduct at CBS; the board said it would investigate. Moonves acknowledged past advances but denied misusing his position.

title: 51 more Tyndall patients sue USC as board chairman pledges expedited inquiry
summary: Fifty-one additional women filed suit against USC and Tyndall, and trustees chairman Rick Caruso said the university's internal investigation would be expedited.

title: Jim Jordan interviewed by investigators in Strauss inquiry
summary: Rep. Jim Jordan was interviewed by the Perkins Coie investigators examining Strauss's conduct.

title: New lawsuit against Ohio State over Strauss names Jim Jordan
summary: A federal lawsuit by former students over Strauss's alleged abuse referenced Jordan among coaches who allegedly knew of complaints.

title: Tyndall retains high-profile criminal defense attorney
summary: Tyndall hired prominent Los Angeles defense lawyer Leonard Levine as police continued their investigation and civil suits mounted.

title: House Speaker Paul Ryan defends Jim Jordan amid Strauss allegations
summary: Speaker Paul Ryan called Jordan a man of integrity and discouraged a House Ethics inquiry into whether he knew of the abuse.

title: Ex-athletes describe years of alleged misconduct by Ohio State doctor
summary: Former Ohio State athletes described alleged abuse by Strauss spanning years, and said complaints were widely known in athletic facilities.

title: New voyeurism claims at Ohio State facility test Jordan's denials
summary: Former wrestlers described a pattern of harassment and voyeurism at Larkins Hall, adding pressure on Rep. Jim Jordan's denials.

title: Former Fox executive Bill Shine named White House communications chief
summary: Shine, who left Fox amid criticism of how he handled harassment complaints under Ailes, was appointed to a senior White House communications post.

title: Jim Jordan denies knowing of Strauss abuse
summary: Rep. Jim Jordan said no athlete ever reported abuse to him and denied any knowledge of misconduct by Strauss.

title: Former wrestlers allege Rep. Jim Jordan ignored Strauss abuse as assistant coach
summary: Former Ohio State wrestlers alleged that U.S. Rep. Jim Jordan, an assistant wrestling coach from 1986 to 1994, knew of Strauss's conduct and did not act. Jordan has denied the allegations.

title: Weinstein indicted on additional charges involving a third woman
summary: Prosecutors added charges including predatory sexual assault, which carries a potential life sentence, based on an allegation from a third woman.

title: Strauss inquiry expanded to include examinations of high school students
summary: Investigators broadened the Strauss probe to cover examinations he performed on high school students.

title: Spanier loses state appeal of child endangerment conviction
summary: A Pennsylvania Superior Court panel upheld Spanier's misdemeanor conviction.

title: At least 200 former students join lawsuits against USC over Tyndall
summary: The number of former students suing USC grew to at least 200, alleging the university ignored warnings about Tyndall for nearly 30 years.

title: Cardinal Theodore McCarrick removed from public ministry after abuse allegation found credible
summary: The Vatican ordered retired Washington Archbishop Theodore McCarrick out of public ministry after an Archdiocese of New York review board found credible a decades-old allegation that he abused a teenage altar server. McCarrick denied the allegation.

title: LAPD serves search warrants at ex-USC gynecologist's home and storage unit
summary: Police detectives searched Tyndall's Los Angeles home and a storage facility as part of the criminal investigation into allegations from former patients.

title: Eight more members of Oxford grooming ring jailed
summary: Eight men were jailed for sexual offences against girls in Oxford in a follow-up phase of the Bullfinch investigation.

title: Pope accepts resignations of Barros and two other Chilean bishops
summary: Francis accepted the first three resignations, including that of Bishop Barros of Osorno.

title: Federal Education Department opens investigation into USC's handling of Tyndall complaints
summary: The U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights began investigating whether USC violated Title IX in responding to complaints about its campus gynecologist.

title: Former USA Gymnastics chief Steve Penny invokes the Fifth before Senate panel
summary: At a Senate subcommittee hearing on the Nassar case, Penny declined to answer questions, while Lou Anna Simon and other officials testified.

title: Weinstein pleads not guilty to rape and sex abuse charges
summary: Weinstein entered a not guilty plea in Manhattan court, and his lawyer said he would seek to have the case dismissed.

title: Manhattan grand jury indicts Weinstein on rape and sex crime charges
summary: A grand jury returned an indictment against Weinstein on rape and criminal sexual act charges, formalizing the case brought by the Manhattan district attorney.

title: USC President C.L. Max Nikias agrees to step down
summary: USC's board of trustees announced that Nikias would step down as president amid mounting pressure over the university's handling of the Tyndall complaints.

title: More women sue USC as Tyndall defends himself in letter to The Times
summary: Fourteen more women filed lawsuits alleging Tyndall abused them during exams and that USC ignored complaints, while Tyndall denied wrongdoing in a letter to the newspaper.

title: Harvey Weinstein surrenders to New York police and is charged with rape
summary: Weinstein turned himself in at a Manhattan precinct and was charged with rape and a criminal sexual act involving two women; he was released on $1 million bail.

title: About 300 former patients come forward as LAPD begins Tyndall investigation
summary: Roughly 300 people contacted USC about Tyndall and the university began sharing patient information with the Los Angeles Police Department, which opened a criminal investigation.

title: Records show students warned USC about gynecologist early in his career
summary: Former patients said they complained to USC about Tyndall as early as the 1990s, suggesting the university missed early chances to act.

title: USC Academic Senate calls on Nikias to resign
summary: USC's faculty governing body voted to call for President Nikias's resignation following the Tyndall revelations and a series of other campus scandals.

title: Ohio State president emails alumni seeking information on Strauss
summary: President Michael Drake contacted more than 100,000 alumni asking anyone with information about Strauss to contact the investigators.

title: Archbishop Philip Wilson found guilty of concealing child sexual abuse
summary: Adelaide's archbishop became the most senior Catholic cleric convicted of concealing abuse, over a priest's crimes in the 1970s in New South Wales.

title: 200 USC professors demand President Nikias resign over Tyndall handling
summary: Two hundred USC faculty members signed a letter calling for President C.L. Max Nikias to step down, while the board of trustees initially expressed confidence in him.

title: USC fires two health clinic supervisors amid gynecologist scandal
summary: USC dismissed two supervisors at its student health center over their handling of complaints about Tyndall as reports from former patients poured in.

title: All of Chile's bishops offer their resignations
summary: Following meetings with the pope in Rome, all 34 active Chilean bishops tendered their resignations over abuse and cover-up.

title: Fox News pays $10 million to settle 18 discrimination and harassment suits
summary: Fox News paid about $10 million to resolve 18 race and gender discrimination claims brought by current and former employees.

title: Michigan State agrees to $500 million settlement with Nassar survivors
summary: MSU agreed to pay $500 million to settle claims from 332 people, the largest settlement of its kind involving a university.

title: LA Times reveals USC let gynecologist keep treating students despite years of complaints
summary: A Los Angeles Times investigation reported that USC received complaints for decades about campus gynecologist George Tyndall's conduct toward young women but allowed him to keep practicing and quietly let him resign in 2017 without reporting him to the medical board.

title: Former USC students describe decades of troubling conduct by campus gynecologist
summary: Former patients spanning several decades told the Times about inappropriate comments and examinations by Tyndall, broadening the account of his time at the student health center.

title: NBC internal review of Lauer finds no evidence news leadership knew of misconduct
summary: An NBC Universal internal investigation concluded that senior news executives were not aware of complaints about Matt Lauer before November 2017 and found no culture of harassment, a finding critics questioned because it was not independent.

title: Bankruptcy judge approves sale of Weinstein Company assets to Lantern Capital
summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge approved the sale of the studio's film and television assets to Lantern Capital Partners for roughly $289 million.

title: Strauss investigation widens as more former athletes from several sports come forward
summary: Ohio State said additional allegations against Strauss had emerged from athletes in multiple sports, and outside law firm Perkins Coie was leading the independent investigation.

title: Temple University rescinds Bill Cosby's honorary degree after conviction
summary: Temple's board voted to revoke the honorary degree it awarded Cosby, joining numerous other colleges that withdrew honors after his conviction.

title: Bill Cosby convicted on three counts of aggravated indecent assault at retrial
summary: A jury in Norristown, Pennsylvania, found Cosby guilty of drugging and sexually assaulting Andrea Constand in 2004, making him the first celebrity convicted in the #MeToo era.

title: Inquiry publishes report on Rochdale and Cyril Smith-era institutions
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry found Rochdale council failed boys abused at Knowl View school and Cambridge House hostel and criticised the handling of allegations against MP Cyril Smith.

title: Prosecutors disclose Cosby paid Constand nearly $3.4 million in 2006 civil settlement
summary: During opening statements at the retrial, prosecutors revealed that Cosby paid about $3.38 million to settle Constand's civil lawsuit in 2006.

title: Pope admits grave errors in handling Chile abuse crisis
summary: After reading Scicluna's report, Francis wrote to Chile's bishops acknowledging serious mistakes caused by a lack of truthful information and summoned them to Rome.

title: Ohio State opens investigation into abuse claims against late team doctor Richard Strauss
summary: Ohio State announced an investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct by Richard Strauss, a former wrestling team physician who died in 2005, and asked former students and coaches to come forward.

title: Weinstein Company files for bankruptcy and releases accusers from nondisclosure agreements
summary: The Weinstein Company filed for Chapter 11 protection in Delaware with a stalking-horse bid from Lantern Capital and said it was ending nondisclosure agreements that had kept accusers silent.

title: Judge allows five additional accusers to testify at Cosby retrial
summary: The trial judge ruled that five other women could testify about alleged prior misconduct at Cosby's retrial, a significant expansion from the single additional accuser allowed in the first trial.

title: Sunday Mirror alleges up to 1,000 girls exploited in Telford
summary: A Sunday Mirror investigation alleged that as many as 1,000 girls may have been abused in Telford over decades, prompting calls for an independent inquiry.

title: Aly Raisman sues U.S. Olympic Committee and USA Gymnastics
summary: Raisman filed suit alleging the USOC and USA Gymnastics knew or should have known about Nassar's abuse and failed to stop it.

title: New York attorney general sues Weinstein Company and Harvey and Bob Weinstein
summary: Attorney General Eric Schneiderman filed a civil rights suit alleging the company failed to protect employees from Harvey Weinstein's harassment, derailing a pending sale of the studio.

title: Michigan State moves to fire former medical dean William Strampel
summary: MSU began proceedings to fire William Strampel, Nassar's former dean at the College of Osteopathic Medicine, over his oversight of Nassar.

title: Nassar sentenced to 40 to 125 years in Eaton County
summary: Judge Janice Cunningham imposed a third prison sentence on Nassar for abuse at the Twistars gym, concluding his criminal cases.

title: Pope sends Archbishop Scicluna to investigate Chile abuse claims
summary: The Vatican dispatched its top abuse investigator to gather testimony about Barros and the Karadima circle.

title: Former governor John Engler named interim MSU president
summary: Michigan State trustees chose former Michigan governor John Engler as interim president following Simon's resignation, a choice some survivors opposed.

title: House passes Safe Sport bill on mandatory abuse reporting
summary: The House approved the Protecting Young Victims from Sexual Abuse and Safe Sport Authorization Act, which became law in February 2018.

title: ESPN reports pattern of denial and inaction at Michigan State
summary: An Outside the Lines investigation reported that Michigan State had a broader pattern of mishandling sexual assault complaints across its athletics programs.

title: Michigan attorney general launches investigation into MSU
summary: Michigan's attorney general announced an independent investigation into how Michigan State handled complaints about Nassar.

title: Entire USA Gymnastics board agrees to resign after USOC demand
summary: The remaining USA Gymnastics directors agreed to step down after the U.S. Olympic Committee threatened to decertify the organization.

title: Nassar sentenced to 40 to 175 years in state prison
summary: Judge Aquilina sentenced Nassar to 40 to 175 years in prison in Ingham County after a week of survivor testimony.

title: Michigan State President Lou Anna Simon resigns
summary: Simon resigned under pressure from lawmakers, survivors and faculty over the university's handling of complaints about Nassar.

title: Top USA Gymnastics board members resign
summary: USA Gymnastics' chairman, vice chairman and treasurer resigned amid mounting criticism during Nassar's sentencing hearing.

title: Pope's defense of Bishop Barros causes outrage
summary: Francis said accusations against Barros were slander absent proof, angering survivors; he later apologized for the remark.

title: Olympian Jordyn Wieber says she was also abused by Nassar
summary: Olympic gold medalist Jordyn Wieber disclosed in court during the sentencing hearing that Nassar had abused her.

title: Detroit News: at least 14 MSU representatives were warned about Nassar
summary: A Detroit News investigation found that at least 14 Michigan State employees, including coaches and trainers, received reports about Nassar over two decades, and that President Lou Anna Simon was told of a 2014 complaint.

title: USA Gymnastics cuts ties with Karolyi Ranch training center
summary: USA Gymnastics ended its agreement to use the Karolyi Ranch in Texas as the national team training center, where athletes said Nassar abused them.

title: Nassar sentencing hearing opens with victim impact statements
summary: Judge Rosemarie Aquilina opened a multi-day sentencing hearing in Ingham County at which more than 150 survivors ultimately gave statements.

title: Simone Biles says she was abused by Nassar
summary: Four-time Olympic champion Simone Biles said she was among the athletes abused by Nassar and called for accountability from USA Gymnastics.

title: Penn State settles suit alleging Sandusky abuse in 2007
summary: Penn State settled a lawsuit by an anonymous plaintiff who alleged Sandusky abused him in 2007, shortly before the case was set for trial.

title: Maggie Nichols says she was first to report Nassar to USA Gymnastics
summary: Elite gymnast Maggie Nichols revealed she was the athlete whose 2015 report first alerted USA Gymnastics to Nassar, and said she was discouraged from speaking out.

title: Maroney lawsuit says USA Gymnastics used a confidentiality deal to silence her
summary: McKayla Maroney sued USA Gymnastics, the U.S. Olympic Committee and Michigan State, alleging a 2016 settlement with a nondisclosure clause was used to keep her abuse quiet.

title: Royal commission final report; church leaders reject key recommendations
institution: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The royal commission's final report made hundreds of recommendations, including on the confessional seal and celibacy, which Catholic leaders rejected.

title: Nassar sentenced to 60 years in federal prison on child pornography counts
summary: A federal judge sentenced Nassar to the maximum 60 years in prison on the child pornography charges, to be served before any state sentences.

title: Netflix fires Danny Masterson from 'The Ranch' amid rape allegations
summary: Netflix wrote actor Danny Masterson out of The Ranch after several women accused him of rape and alleged the LAPD investigation had stalled. Masterson denied the allegations.

title: 20th Century Fox fires Bryan Singer as director of 'Bohemian Rhapsody'
summary: Fox removed Bryan Singer from the Queen biopic mid-production, citing his absences from set, days before a lawsuit accusing him of sexual assault was filed. Singer disputed the studio's account.

title: NBC fires 'Today' anchor Matt Lauer over sexual misconduct complaint
summary: NBC News fired longtime Today co-anchor Matt Lauer after a colleague filed a detailed complaint of inappropriate sexual behavior, saying it had reason to believe it was not an isolated incident.

title: Nassar pleads guilty to three more sexual assault counts in Eaton County
summary: Nassar pleaded guilty to three additional counts in Eaton County related to abuse at the Twistars gymnastics club.

title: Nassar pleads guilty to criminal sexual conduct in Ingham County
summary: Nassar pleaded guilty to seven counts of first-degree criminal sexual conduct in Ingham County, admitting to abusing patients under the guise of treatment.

title: 21st Century Fox agrees to $90 million shareholder settlement and workplace council
summary: Fox settled a shareholder derivative suit over board oversight of harassment for $90 million and agreed to create a Fox News Workplace Professionalism and Inclusion Council.

title: Gabby Douglas says she was also abused by Nassar
summary: Olympic all-around champion Gabby Douglas said she too had been abused by the national team doctor.

title: Senate passes bill requiring amateur sports bodies to report sexual abuse
summary: The Senate passed legislation requiring Olympic governing bodies and their members to promptly report suspected abuse and strengthening the U.S. Center for SafeSport.

title: Penn State's Sandusky-related costs exceed a quarter-billion dollars
summary: New payments of about $16 million raised Penn State's total settlements with Sandusky claimants to about $109 million, and overall scandal costs to more than $250 million.

title: Olympic captain Aly Raisman says she was abused by Nassar
summary: Two-time Olympic team captain Aly Raisman said publicly that Nassar abused her and criticized USA Gymnastics' response.

title: Report says Weinstein hired private intelligence firms to monitor accusers and journalists
summary: A follow-up New Yorker report alleged Weinstein used private investigators, including an Israeli intelligence firm, to gather information on accusers and reporters in an effort to suppress the stories.

title: McQueary ends whistleblower lawsuit after settlement with Penn State
summary: McQueary and Penn State resolved his litigation, ending appeals of the roughly $12 million judgment; terms were not immediately disclosed.

title: Netflix cuts ties with Kevin Spacey, drops him from 'House of Cards'
summary: Netflix said it would no longer work with Kevin Spacey and would not move forward with House of Cards involving him, as further misconduct allegations emerged from people who worked on the show.

title: Kevin Spacey accused by Anthony Rapp of advance when Rapp was 14; Spacey apologizes
summary: Actor Anthony Rapp publicly alleged that Kevin Spacey made a sexual advance toward him in 1986, when Rapp was a teenager. Spacey said he did not remember the encounter and apologized.

title: Report: O'Reilly settled analyst's harassment claim for $32 million before contract renewal
summary: The Times reported O'Reilly paid about $32 million in January 2017 to settle claims by a longtime Fox legal analyst, and that Fox renewed his contract weeks later knowing of the deal.

title: Judge denies Sandusky's bid for a new trial under post-conviction law
summary: After hearings on claims of ineffective counsel and other issues, a judge rejected Sandusky's post-conviction petition for a new trial.

title: Olympic champion McKayla Maroney says Nassar abused her
summary: Olympic gold medalist McKayla Maroney said in a #MeToo post that Nassar abused her for years, beginning when she was on the national team.

title: Harvey Weinstein resigns from Weinstein Company board
summary: Weinstein stepped down from the board of the company he co-founded, cutting his last formal role there.

title: #MeToo goes viral as women share experiences in wake of Weinstein revelations
summary: Actress Alyssa Milano invited people who had experienced sexual harassment or assault to reply 'me too,' and the hashtag, building on activist Tarana Burke's earlier campaign, spread to millions of posts amid the Weinstein coverage.

title: Motion Picture Academy expels Harvey Weinstein
summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences board voted to expel Weinstein, an unusual step for the organization that oversees the Oscars.

title: NYPD opens review of sexual assault allegations against Weinstein
summary: The New York Police Department said it was reviewing allegations against Weinstein, and London police also began examining a complaint.

title: New Yorker report adds allegations of sexual assault against Weinstein
summary: A New Yorker investigation by Ronan Farrow included accounts from multiple women alleging sexual assault, including rape, by Weinstein, as more actresses came forward with their own accounts.

title: Weinstein Company board fires co-founder Harvey Weinstein
summary: The Weinstein Company's board terminated Harvey Weinstein, citing new information about his conduct that had emerged in the preceding days.

title: NYT investigation reveals decades of harassment allegations and settlements involving Harvey Weinstein
summary: The New York Times reported that Harvey Weinstein had faced harassment allegations over nearly three decades and had reached private settlements with several accusers; actress Ashley Judd was among those who spoke on the record.

title: Harvey Weinstein announces leave of absence from his company after harassment report
summary: Following the Times report, Weinstein said he would take a leave from The Weinstein Company, while his lawyers disputed parts of the story.

title: Commentator Scottie Nell Hughes sues Fox, alleging rape by host Charles Payne
summary: Political commentator Scottie Nell Hughes sued Fox News alleging Fox Business host Charles Payne sexually assaulted her and the network retaliated after she ended their relationship. Payne denied the allegations.

title: Eric Bolling leaves Fox News after harassment investigation
summary: Fox News and Bolling agreed to part ways following the network's investigation into the allegations against him.

title: Fox News suspends host Eric Bolling over alleged lewd messages
summary: Fox suspended Bolling pending an investigation into a report that he sent an explicit photo to female colleagues. Bolling denied the allegation.

title: Curley and Schultz report to jail
summary: The two former administrators surrendered at the Centre County Correctional Facility to begin their sentences.

title: Nassar pleads guilty to federal child pornography charges
summary: Nassar pleaded guilty in federal court in Grand Rapids to three child pornography counts as part of a plea agreement.

title: Paterno family drops lawsuit against the NCAA
summary: Paterno's estate, his son Jay and a former assistant discontinued their suit against the NCAA over its use of the Freeh Report; the NCAA said no payment was made.

title: Cardinal George Pell charged with historical sexual offences
summary: Victoria Police charged Pell, the Vatican's finance chief, with historical sexual offences; he denied the allegations and took leave to fight them.

title: Cosby trial ends in mistrial after jury deadlocks
summary: A judge declared a mistrial in Cosby's first criminal trial after jurors deadlocked following six days of deliberations; prosecutors said they would retry the case.

title: Spanier, Curley and Schultz sentenced to jail terms
summary: A judge sentenced the three former administrators to jail terms of at least two months each, followed by house arrest, for failing to alert authorities about the 2001 allegation.

title: Former Fox News chairman Roger Ailes dies at 77
summary: Ailes died less than a year after his ouster over harassment allegations, which he had denied; several related lawsuits remained pending.

title: Accusers testify against Nassar at preliminary examination
summary: Three women testified at a preliminary hearing in Ingham County, after which Nassar was ordered to stand trial on state sexual assault charges.

title: Fox News co-president Bill Shine resigns amid scrutiny of harassment handling
summary: Shine, a longtime Ailes deputy criticized in lawsuits for his handling of harassment complaints, resigned as co-president of Fox News.

title: Federal probe of Fox News expands to include postal inspectors
summary: The Justice Department inquiry into Fox News was reported to have broadened beyond Ailes-era harassment settlements, with Postal Inspection Service financial investigators involved.

title: Bill O'Reilly ousted from Fox News after harassment allegations
summary: 21st Century Fox ended O'Reilly's tenure after a review of harassment allegations and an advertiser exodus from his top-rated show.

title: New lawsuits against Nassar and MSU include allegations dating to 1992
summary: Four more complaints were filed in the growing civil litigation against Nassar, Michigan State and others, with one alleging abuse as early as 1992.

title: Michigan board suspends Nassar's medical license
source: Detroit Free Press / Lansing State Journal
summary: Michigan's osteopathic medicine licensing board revoked Nassar's medical license for at least three years while criminal cases were pending.

title: Times report finds $13 million in settlements tied to Bill O'Reilly
summary: A New York Times investigation found that O'Reilly or Fox had paid about $13 million to settle claims from five women accusing him of harassment or inappropriate behavior. O'Reilly denied wrongdoing.

title: Jury convicts Graham Spanier of one count of child endangerment
summary: A Dauphin County jury found former president Spanier guilty of a misdemeanor child endangerment count over his handling of the 2001 report, while acquitting him of conspiracy and a second endangerment count.

title: USA Gymnastics president Steve Penny resigns
summary: Steve Penny resigned as president and CEO of USA Gymnastics under pressure from the U.S. Olympic Committee over the organization's handling of abuse complaints.

title: Curley and Schultz plead guilty to misdemeanor child endangerment
summary: Former athletic director Tim Curley and former vice president Gary Schultz pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor count of endangering the welfare of children, and agreed to testify at Spanier's trial.

title: Significant quantities of infant remains found at former Tuam home
institution: Mother and Baby Homes Commission of Investigation
summary: The state commission confirmed test excavations found significant human remains in underground chambers at the former Tuam mother and baby home.

title: Judge orders release of USA Gymnastics sexual misconduct complaint files
summary: A judge granted the IndyStar's request to unseal USA Gymnastics files on complaints against coaches, showing how the organization handled years of allegations.

title: Survivor Marie Collins quits Vatican abuse commission citing resistance
summary: Collins resigned, saying Vatican offices resisted the commission's recommendations.

title: Nassar faces 22 additional sexual assault charges in Michigan
summary: Michigan prosecutors filed 22 more counts of criminal sexual conduct against Nassar in Ingham and Eaton counties, involving patients he treated at MSU and a local gym.

title: Former national team gymnasts describe Nassar abuse on 60 Minutes
summary: Former U.S. national team gymnasts, including Olympian Jamie Dantzscher, publicly alleged on 60 Minutes that Nassar abused them and that the national team environment enabled it.

title: Royal commission data shows Australian church paid $276m to abuse victims
institution: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Hearings revealed thousands of claims against Catholic institutions and that about 7% of priests between 1950 and 2010 were alleged perpetrators.

title: USA Gymnastics says it alerted the FBI to Nassar in 2015
summary: USA Gymnastics disclosed that it reported concerns about Nassar to the FBI in mid-2015, more than a year before he was publicly accused, raising questions about the bureau's handling.

title: Federal prosecutors investigate Fox News over Ailes-era settlement payments
summary: The U.S. Attorney's office in Manhattan was reported to be examining whether Fox News properly disclosed harassment settlement payments to investors.

title: MSU gymnasts say they were told not to talk to police about Nassar
summary: A Michigan State gymnast alleged that team members were discouraged from speaking to police investigating Nassar, raising questions about the university's response.

title: Michigan State gymnastics coach Kathie Klages resigns over Nassar fallout
summary: Longtime MSU gymnastics coach Kathie Klages resigned after being suspended, while denying she knew of abuse by Nassar.

title: Rochdale grooming gang members lose bid to avoid deportation
summary: A tribunal ruled that four members of the Rochdale gang could be stripped of British citizenship and face deportation to Pakistan.

title: Rolf Harris cleared of further sex assault charges
summary: A jury cleared Rolf Harris of three indecent assault charges and failed to reach verdicts on four others; prosecutors later decided not to seek a retrial.

title: Nassar indicted on federal child pornography charges
summary: A federal grand jury in Michigan indicted Nassar on charges of receiving and possessing child sexual abuse images, after agents seized material from his home.

title: IndyStar finds 368 gymnasts alleged sexual abuse over 20 years
summary: A follow-up IndyStar investigation documented allegations from at least 368 gymnasts against coaches and other adults across the U.S. gymnastics system over two decades.

title: Judge rules for McQueary on whistleblower claim, adding $5 million in damages
summary: A judge found Penn State retaliated against McQueary under the state whistleblower law and awarded about $5 million more, bringing the total to roughly $12 million.

title: Michigan attorney general files first sexual assault charges against Nassar
summary: Michigan Attorney General Bill Schuette charged Nassar with criminal sexual conduct involving a minor, calling the case the tip of the iceberg. Nassar pleaded not guilty.

title: Survivors' group withdraws from the inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Shirley Oaks Survivors Association, representing hundreds of people abused in Lambeth care, withdrew from the inquiry, citing a loss of confidence.

title: Education Department fines Penn State record $2.4 million for Clery Act violations
summary: After a five-year investigation, the Department of Education issued a record Clery Act fine, finding Penn State failed to properly report campus crimes and warn of threats, including in the Sandusky matter.

title: Jury awards Mike McQueary $7.3 million in defamation case against Penn State
summary: A Centre County jury found Penn State liable for defaming and misrepresenting McQueary and awarded him $7.3 million.

title: Lead counsel Ben Emmerson QC resigns from inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry's senior lawyer resigned after being suspended over leadership concerns, adding to turmoil at the inquiry.

title: More women come forward with abuse allegations against Nassar
summary: Additional former patients, including athletes treated at Michigan State, came forward alleging abuse by Nassar. Police and the university opened investigations.

title: Penn State settles coverage fight with its insurer
summary: Penn State and insurer PMA settled their litigation over who would pay for Sandusky-related settlements, ending a case that had surfaced new allegations.

title: Michigan State University fires Larry Nassar amid abuse allegations
summary: Michigan State University fired Nassar, a faculty physician, after allegations from gymnasts and other patients. The university said he had violated requirements imposed after an earlier complaint.

title: Former USA Gymnastics team doctor Larry Nassar accused of sexual abuse by two gymnasts
summary: Former gymnast Rachael Denhollander and an unnamed Olympic medalist accused longtime national team physician Larry Nassar of sexually abusing them during treatments. Nassar denied wrongdoing.

title: Fox News pays Gretchen Carlson $20 million to settle harassment suit
summary: 21st Century Fox settled Carlson's lawsuit for a reported $20 million and issued a public apology, an unusual step for the company.

title: Former Fox host Andrea Tantaros sues network over alleged harassment and retaliation
summary: Former host Andrea Tantaros sued Fox News, Ailes and other executives, alleging sexual harassment and retaliation after she complained. Fox denied the claims.

title: Professor Alexis Jay named fourth chair of abuse inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Alexis Jay, author of the Rotherham report and an existing panel member, was appointed to lead the inquiry.

title: Dame Lowell Goddard resigns as inquiry chair
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Goddard became the third chair to resign, stepping down by letter after 18 months amid reports of internal difficulties.

title: IndyStar investigation finds USA Gymnastics failed to report abuse complaints against coaches
summary: An Indianapolis Star investigation reported that USA Gymnastics routinely failed to alert authorities to sexual misconduct complaints against coaches. The series prompted the first public accusations against team doctor Larry Nassar.

title: Former Fox booker says Ailes harassed her for two decades
summary: A former Fox News booker told New York magazine that Ailes harassed and psychologically controlled her for about 20 years and that the network helped conceal it.

title: Roger Ailes resigns as Fox News chairman amid harassment claims
summary: Ailes stepped down as chairman and CEO of Fox News after an internal investigation into harassment allegations, with Rupert Murdoch taking over as acting chief.

title: Megyn Kelly reportedly told Fox investigators that Ailes harassed her
summary: Reports said anchor Megyn Kelly told the outside law firm reviewing Carlson's claims that Ailes had made unwanted advances toward her years earlier.

title: Unsealed records detail claims that Penn State coaches heard of Sandusky abuse decades earlier
summary: Documents unsealed in the insurance litigation included testimony alleging that Paterno and other coaches were told of abuse by Sandusky as early as the 1970s and 1980s. The claims were untested in court.

title: Gretchen Carlson sues Fox News chief Roger Ailes for sexual harassment
summary: Former Fox News anchor Gretchen Carlson filed suit alleging that chairman Roger Ailes sexually harassed her and ended her contract after she rebuffed him. Ailes denied the allegations.

title: Abuse allegations follow Sodalitium founder Figari to Rome
summary: Former members accused Luis Fernando Figari, founder of the Peru-based Sodalitium Christianae Vitae, of sexual and psychological abuse; he denied wrongdoing.

title: Judge orders Cosby to stand trial after preliminary hearing
summary: A district judge found enough evidence for Cosby's sexual assault case to proceed to trial on three felony counts of aggravated indecent assault.

title: Insurance case filing alleges Paterno was told of Sandusky abuse in 1976
summary: A judge's order in Penn State's coverage dispute with its insurer referenced an allegation that a boy complained to Paterno about Sandusky in 1976. Paterno's family disputed the claim.

title: Ten men jailed for sex offences against girls in Rochdale
summary: Ten men were jailed following a further Greater Manchester Police investigation into the sexual exploitation of girls in Rochdale.

title: Sandusky's Second Mile charity dissolves with court approval
summary: A judge approved the dissolution of The Second Mile, the youth charity Sandusky founded, after it had wound down its programs following his arrest.

title: Dame Janet Smith review finds BBC culture let Savile and Hall abuse unchecked
summary: The Dame Janet Smith review found Savile abused 72 people connected to the BBC and that a culture of fear and deference meant staff concerns went unreported; the BBC apologised.

title: Appeals court throws out some charges against Spanier, Curley and Schultz
summary: The Superior Court dismissed perjury, obstruction and conspiracy charges after finding the university's former general counsel improperly testified before the grand jury, leaving child endangerment counts intact.

title: Bill Cosby charged with felony aggravated indecent assault in 2004 Constand case
summary: Montgomery County prosecutors charged Cosby with aggravated indecent assault over the 2004 encounter with former Temple employee Andrea Constand, days before the statute of limitations was set to expire.

title: Inquiry announces investigations into MPs, councils and churches
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry named its first 12 investigations, including Westminster, the Anglican and Catholic churches, Lambeth and Nottinghamshire councils and Rochdale.

title: Penn State's Sandusky settlements total about $93 million
summary: University financial disclosures showed Penn State had paid nearly $93 million to settle claims from 33 people abused by Sandusky.

title: Court orders Sandusky's state pension restored
summary: A Commonwealth Court panel ruled the State Employees' Retirement Board wrongly revoked Sandusky's roughly $4,900-a-month pension.

title: Police chief says Operation Yewtree 'got things wrong'
summary: A senior police leader acknowledged mistakes in Operation Yewtree, including the handling of high-profile people who were arrested but never charged.

title: Prosecutor whose campaign focused on Cosby case wins Montgomery County DA race
summary: Kevin Steele defeated former DA Bruce Castor, who had declined to charge Cosby in 2005, in a race where the Cosby case became a central campaign issue.

title: New York magazine cover story gathers 35 women accusing Cosby
summary: New York magazine published a cover story featuring 35 women who accuse Cosby of sexual assault, describing their experiences and the silence that followed. Cosby denied wrongdoing.

title: Statutory child sexual abuse inquiry formally opens
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Justice Goddard formally opened the inquiry, setting out a programme expected to examine institutions across England and Wales.

title: Unsealed 2005 deposition shows Cosby admitted obtaining Quaaludes to give women
summary: A federal judge unsealed portions of Cosby's deposition from the Constand civil case, in which he acknowledged obtaining sedatives to give to women he wanted to have sex with.

title: National Crime Agency's Rotherham inquiry identifies 300 suspects
summary: The National Crime Agency's Operation Stovewood said it had identified around 300 possible suspects in historical Rotherham exploitation cases.

title: Protests erupt over installation of Bishop Juan Barros in Osorno
summary: Protesters disrupted the installation of Barros, a Karadima protégé whom survivors accused of witnessing and covering up abuse, which he denied.

title: Greater Manchester Police apologise over Rochdale failures
summary: Greater Manchester Police apologised for failings in the Rochdale investigation, while saying no officers would face criminal charges.

title: Oxfordshire serious case review estimates 373 children groomed
summary: A serious case review found police and social services in Oxfordshire failed to act on clear signs of exploitation and estimated up to 373 children may have been targeted.

title: Gary Glitter jailed for 16 years for abusing girls
summary: Gary Glitter, the first person arrested under Operation Yewtree, was sentenced to 16 years after being convicted of sexually abusing three girls in the 1970s and 1980s.

title: Lampard lessons-learned report and NHS findings on Savile published
summary: Reports into Savile's activities at Stoke Mandeville and dozens of other hospitals found complaints about him were ignored, and a lessons-learned review urged tighter controls on celebrity and volunteer access.

title: Rotherham council accepts Casey inspection findings as commissioners take over
summary: Louise Casey's inspection found Rotherham council not fit for purpose; its cabinet resigned and the government sent in commissioners to run the authority.

title: New Zealand judge Lowell Goddard to lead statutory abuse inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Dame Lowell Goddard was appointed chair and the inquiry was given statutory powers to compel witnesses and evidence.

title: Spanish judge charges 10 priests in Granada abuse case
summary: A Granada judge charged priests and a layman after a former altar boy wrote to Pope Francis, who encouraged him to go to authorities.

title: NCAA settlement restores 111 Paterno wins and keeps $60 million fine in Pennsylvania
summary: Settling a lawsuit by state Sen. Jake Corman, the NCAA restored the vacated wins and agreed the $60 million fine would fund child abuse prevention programs in Pennsylvania.

title: U.S. Virgin Islands reviews Epstein donations to local students
summary: Virgin Islands officials began reviewing Epstein's donations to young students in the territory amid renewed attention to his abuse allegations.

title: Ireland publishes terms of mother and baby homes inquiry
institution: Mother and Baby Homes Commission of Investigation
summary: The Irish government set the terms of a commission to investigate 14 mother and baby homes and four county homes, prompted by the Tuam revelations.

title: Court filing accuses Ghislaine Maxwell and alleges Prince Andrew links in Epstein case
summary: Filings in a federal Crime Victims' Rights Act case challenging Epstein's plea deal alleged that Maxwell recruited girls and that Prince Andrew was involved; both denied the allegations.

title: Theresa May reported to scrap original inquiry panel
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The home secretary was reported to be disbanding the original panel and reconstituting the inquiry with stronger powers.

title: Court of Appeal approves compensation scheme for Savile victims
summary: The Court of Appeal rejected a challenge by the Jimmy Savile Charitable Trust and approved a compensation scheme for people who say Savile abused them, paid from his estate.

title: Bill Cosby resigns from Temple University board of trustees
summary: Cosby stepped down from Temple University's board of trustees, where he had served for decades, as sexual assault allegations against him multiplied.

title: NBC scraps planned Cosby sitcom and TV Land pulls reruns amid mounting allegations
summary: NBC dropped a family comedy it had been developing with Cosby and TV Land removed The Cosby Show reruns as more women came forward with allegations; Netflix also postponed a planned Cosby special.

title: Actress Barbara Bowman publicly accuses Cosby, asks why earlier claims were ignored
summary: Actress Barbara Bowman wrote a Washington Post op-ed alleging Cosby assaulted her in the 1980s, helping spark a new wave of public accusations. Cosby's representatives denied the claims.

title: Emails show NCAA officials questioned their authority to punish Penn State
summary: Emails released in a state senator's lawsuit showed NCAA staff had doubted whether the association had jurisdiction to sanction Penn State over the Sandusky case.

title: Fiona Woolf resigns as chair of child abuse inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Woolf stepped down after survivors objected to her social links with former home secretary Leon Brittan.

title: Dave Lee Travis found guilty of indecent assault
summary: Former Radio 1 DJ Dave Lee Travis was convicted at a retrial of indecently assaulting a woman in 1995; he later received a suspended sentence.

title: South Yorkshire police commissioner Shaun Wright resigns
summary: Shaun Wright, who oversaw children's services in Rotherham during part of the period examined by the Jay report, resigned as South Yorkshire police and crime commissioner.

title: NCAA lifts Penn State's postseason ban early
summary: The NCAA Executive Committee ended the football postseason ban two years early and said full scholarships would return, citing the university's reforms.

title: Lord Mayor Fiona Woolf named to lead abuse inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: City of London Lord Mayor Fiona Woolf was appointed as the inquiry's second chair.

title: Jay report finds at least 1,400 children exploited in Rotherham
summary: Professor Alexis Jay's independent inquiry estimated at least 1,400 children were sexually exploited in Rotherham between 1997 and 2013 and found council and police leaders failed them.

title: Butler-Sloss steps down from abuse inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Butler-Sloss withdrew as chair after criticism over the fact that her late brother had been attorney general in the 1980s.

title: Baroness Butler-Sloss appointed to head child abuse inquiry
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Former senior judge Baroness Butler-Sloss was named chair of the new inquiry into institutional child sexual abuse.

title: Theresa May announces independent inquiry into institutional child abuse
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Home Secretary Theresa May announced an independent panel inquiry into how public bodies and other institutions handled child sexual abuse, amid claims about historical abuse networks.

title: Rolf Harris jailed for five years and nine months
summary: Entertainer Rolf Harris, long a BBC presenter, was jailed after being convicted of 12 indecent assaults against girls between 1968 and 1986.

title: NHS reports find Savile abused patients aged five to 75 in hospitals
summary: Investigations at Leeds General Infirmary, Broadmoor and other NHS hospitals found Savile abused patients and staff over decades; the health secretary apologised to victims.

title: Attorney general's review finds no political delay in Sandusky prosecution
summary: The Moulton report found no evidence that then-AG Tom Corbett deliberately slowed the Sandusky investigation for political reasons, though Attorney General Kane criticized its pace.

title: Almost 800 infants found buried in unmarked graves at Tuam home
summary: Research by a local historian indicated nearly 800 children who died at a Bon Secours-run mother and baby home in Tuam were buried without markers.

title: Stuart Hall given further jail term after second trial
summary: Stuart Hall received an additional prison sentence after being found guilty at a second trial of indecently assaulting a girl.

title: Max Clifford jailed for eight years
summary: Max Clifford was sentenced to eight years in prison for indecent assaults committed between 1977 and 1984.

title: Max Clifford found guilty of eight indecent assaults
summary: A jury at Southwark Crown Court convicted Max Clifford of eight counts of indecent assault against women and girls.

title: Pope names Cardinal O'Malley and survivors to new anti-abuse commission
summary: Francis appointed the first members of the Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors, including Irish survivor Marie Collins.

title: UN committee demands Vatican remove abusers and open files
institution: UN Committee on the Rights of the Child
summary: The UN Committee on the Rights of the Child sharply criticized the Holy See's handling of clergy abuse and called for abusers to be reported to civil authorities.

title: Leaked draft says Savile may have abused up to 1,000 people on BBC premises
summary: The Observer reported that material gathered for the Dame Janet Smith review suggested the number of people abused by Savile on BBC premises could be far higher than earlier estimates.

title: Report finds police and council errors let Rochdale gangs flourish
summary: Serious case reviews found Greater Manchester Police and Rochdale agencies missed repeated opportunities to protect girls from exploitation.

title: Penn State agrees to pay $59.7 million to 26 Sandusky claimants
summary: Penn State announced settlements totaling $59.7 million with 26 young men who said Sandusky abused them, with several other claims still pending.

title: Savile investigation in the NHS widened to more hospitals
summary: The Department of Health widened its investigation into Savile's activities at NHS hospitals to cover additional sites where he had access.

title: Pennsylvania Superior Court rejects Sandusky's appeal
summary: A three-judge Superior Court panel ruled that Sandusky was not entitled to a new trial, rejecting claims about trial preparation time and prosecutorial remarks.

title: NCAA begins restoring Penn State football scholarships
summary: Citing progress reported by monitor George Mitchell, the NCAA said it would gradually return scholarships cut under the 2012 sanctions.

title: First civil settlement reached between Penn State and a Sandusky victim
summary: A man identified in court papers as Victim 5 completed the first settlement with Penn State after nearly a year of negotiations.

title: Former Radio 1 DJ Dave Lee Travis charged with indecent assault
summary: Prosecutors charged former Radio 1 presenter Dave Lee Travis with indecent assault offences arising from Operation Yewtree.

title: Judge orders Spanier, Curley and Schultz to stand trial
summary: After a preliminary hearing, a district judge ruled prosecutors had presented enough evidence for the three former administrators to face trial on cover-up related charges.

title: Graham Spanier files libel action against Louis Freeh
summary: Spanier initiated a libel and defamation case in Centre County against Freeh over the report's conclusions about his role.

title: Seven members of Oxford abuse ring jailed
summary: The Oxford gang members were sentenced, five of them to life terms, for rape, trafficking and other offences.

title: Stuart Hall jailed for 15 months for indecent assaults
summary: Stuart Hall was sentenced at Preston Crown Court to 15 months in prison; the term was later doubled on appeal as unduly lenient.

title: Federal judge dismisses Corbett's antitrust suit against the NCAA
summary: A federal judge in Harrisburg threw out the governor's lawsuit challenging the Penn State sanctions.

title: Paterno family and others file lawsuit against the NCAA
summary: Paterno's estate, along with some trustees, faculty and former players, sued the NCAA in Centre County, arguing the sanctions based on the Freeh Report violated NCAA rules.

title: Oxford grooming gang convicted after Operation Bullfinch
summary: Seven men were convicted at the Old Bailey of sexually exploiting girls in Oxford over several years following Thames Valley Police's Operation Bullfinch.

title: Operation Chalice trial concludes with convictions in Telford
summary: West Mercia Police's Operation Chalice ended with several men convicted of child sexual exploitation offences against girls in Telford.

title: Veteran BBC broadcaster Stuart Hall admits indecent assaults on girls
summary: Stuart Hall, a longtime BBC presenter, pleaded guilty to 14 counts of indecently assaulting girls between 1967 and 1985.

title: Max Clifford charged with 11 counts of indecent assault
summary: Prosecutors charged Max Clifford with 11 counts of indecent assault following the Operation Yewtree investigation.

title: Penn State sues insurer over coverage of Sandusky-related claims
summary: Penn State sued Pennsylvania Manufacturers' Association Insurance Co., seeking to force the insurer to cover settlements with people abused by Sandusky.

title: Taoiseach issues state apology to Magdalene laundry women
summary: Enda Kenny apologized unreservedly in the Dáil to women held in the laundries and announced a redress scheme.

title: Paterno family releases report challenging Freeh's findings
summary: A review commissioned by Paterno's family, including work by former Gov. Dick Thornburgh, called the Freeh Report's conclusions about Paterno unsupported.

title: McAleese report finds significant state role in Magdalene laundries
institution: Inter-Departmental Committee on the Magdalen Laundries (McAleese Committee)
summary: A government committee found the Irish state was directly involved in sending women and girls to the Catholic-run Magdalene laundries.

title: Attorney General Kane appoints special investigator to review handling of Sandusky probe
summary: Newly elected Attorney General Kathleen Kane named former federal prosecutor Geoffrey Moulton to examine how her predecessors, including then-AG Tom Corbett, conducted the Sandusky investigation.

title: Judge denies Sandusky's request for a new trial
summary: The trial judge rejected Sandusky's post-sentencing motions seeking a new trial, clearing the way for his direct appeal.

title: Police and NSPCC report reveals scale of Savile's offending
summary: The Giving Victims a Voice report by the Metropolitan Police and NSPCC recorded 214 criminal offences by Savile across 28 police force areas over more than five decades.

title: Supreme Court judge named to head abuse royal commission
institution: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The government released terms of reference and named Justice Peter McClellan to chair the six-member royal commission.

title: Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Corbett sues NCAA over Penn State sanctions
summary: Corbett filed a federal antitrust lawsuit seeking to overturn the NCAA's sanctions against Penn State, calling them unlawful and overreaching.

title: Pollard review finds BBC leadership failures over axed Newsnight Savile report
summary: The Pollard review found chaos and leadership failures in the BBC's handling of the dropped Newsnight investigation, though it concluded the decision was not made to protect tribute programmes.

title: Publicist Max Clifford arrested in Yewtree investigation
summary: Publicist Max Clifford was arrested by Operation Yewtree officers on suspicion of sexual offences; he denied the allegations.

title: Survivors welcome national royal commission into institutional child abuse
institution: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Prime Minister Julia Gillard announced a royal commission into institutional responses to child sexual abuse, a move survivors called a bittersweet victory.

title: BBC director general George Entwistle resigns
summary: George Entwistle resigned after 54 days as director general amid the fallout from the shelved Savile report and a separate Newsnight broadcast that wrongly implicated a former politician in abuse.

title: Ex-Penn State president Graham Spanier charged; new counts filed against Curley and Schultz
summary: The state attorney general charged Spanier with perjury, obstruction, conspiracy and child endangerment, and added obstruction and endangerment counts against Curley and Schultz.

title: Gary Glitter arrested by Operation Yewtree detectives
summary: Former pop star Gary Glitter became the first person arrested under Operation Yewtree, the police inquiry prompted by the Savile allegations.

title: Police say number of potential Savile victims reaches 300
summary: The Metropolitan Police said around 300 potential victims had come forward with allegations against Savile spanning several decades.

title: Newsnight editor steps aside over shelved Savile investigation
summary: Newsnight editor Peter Rippon stepped aside after the BBC said his explanation for dropping a 2011 report on Savile abuse allegations had been inaccurate.

title: Metropolitan Police launch Operation Yewtree criminal inquiry
summary: Scotland Yard opened a formal criminal investigation, later known as Operation Yewtree, after concluding some allegations involved people other than Savile who were still alive.

title: More than 1,200 Boy Scouts files on suspected molesters released under court order
summary: Following the Oregon Supreme Court ruling, attorneys made public more than 1,200 Boy Scouts files covering 1965 to 1985. The records showed some removed volunteers rejoined and many allegations were not reported to police, which the Scouts disputed.

title: BBC names Dame Janet Smith and Nick Pollard to lead Savile reviews
summary: The BBC appointed former judge Dame Janet Smith to examine the corporation's culture during Savile's years there and former Sky News chief Nick Pollard to review why Newsnight dropped its Savile report.

title: Penn State declines to renew athletic director Tim Curley's contract
summary: Penn State said it would not renew the contract of Curley, who had been on leave since being charged in 2011.

title: BBC issues apology over Savile and launches two inquiries
summary: BBC director general George Entwistle apologised to those affected and announced reviews into the shelved Newsnight investigation and into the culture of the BBC during Savile's career.

title: Sandusky sentenced to 30 to 60 years in prison
summary: A judge sentenced Sandusky to 30 to 60 years in state prison and designated him a sexually violent predator.

title: Mike McQueary sues Penn State, alleging whistleblower retaliation and defamation
summary: Former assistant coach Mike McQueary sued Penn State, claiming he was mistreated and defamed after he reported the 2001 shower incident and testified against Sandusky.

title: ITV stands by upcoming documentary alleging Jimmy Savile abused teenage girls
summary: ITV defended its forthcoming Exposure documentary alleging the late BBC presenter Jimmy Savile sexually abused girls in the 1970s. The BBC said it had found no record of misconduct on its premises.

title: Times reveals confidential police files on Rotherham child exploitation
summary: The Times reported that confidential police and agency files showed organised sexual exploitation of girls in Rotherham had been known about for years without effective action.

title: Penn State hires Feinberg firm to handle possible settlements with abuse claimants
summary: The university retained Feinberg Rozen LLP, led by mediator Kenneth Feinberg, to help resolve civil claims from people abused by Sandusky.

title: LA Times review of 1,600 files finds Boy Scouts often failed to report suspected abusers
summary: A Los Angeles Times review of about 1,600 confidential files from 1970 to 1991 found Scouting officials often did not alert police and sometimes let accused leaders resign quietly. In many cases where the Scouts learned of abuse first, there was no sign law enforcement was contacted, and some expelled men later rejoined.

title: 422 sex abuse claims filed against the Christian Brothers
summary: Hundreds of abuse claims, many tied to Mount Cashel and other Christian Brothers institutions, were lodged in the order's insolvency proceedings.

title: Accreditor places Penn State on warning over scandal
summary: The Middle States Commission on Higher Education warned that Penn State's accreditation was in jeopardy over governance and integrity issues raised by the scandal. The warning was lifted later that year.

title: NCAA fines Penn State $60 million, imposes bowl ban and vacates 111 wins
summary: Under a consent decree, the NCAA fined Penn State $60 million, banned its football team from the postseason for four years, cut scholarships and vacated wins dating to 1998.

title: Penn State removes Joe Paterno statue outside Beaver Stadium
summary: President Rodney Erickson ordered the statue of Joe Paterno taken down in the wake of the Freeh Report's findings.

title: Freeh Report finds top Penn State officials concealed Sandusky allegations
summary: The Freeh investigation concluded that Paterno, Spanier, Curley and Schultz showed disregard for child victims and concealed facts about Sandusky to avoid bad publicity. Paterno's family and the accused officials disputed the findings.

title: Jury convicts Jerry Sandusky on 45 of 48 counts of child sexual abuse
summary: A Centre County jury found Sandusky guilty of 45 counts involving the abuse of 10 boys over 15 years, and he was jailed pending sentencing.

title: Oregon Supreme Court clears release of 20,000 pages of Boy Scouts 'perversion files'
summary: The Oregon Supreme Court approved public release of roughly 20,000 pages of Boy Scouts files on suspected molesters that had been trial evidence in the 2010 Portland case. It was the first time the public would be able to review the records.

title: Jerry Sandusky's criminal trial begins in Bellefonte
summary: Sandusky's trial opened in Centre County, with prosecutors presenting testimony from men who said he abused them as boys.

title: Rochdale grooming gang members jailed
summary: The nine Rochdale men were sentenced to terms of up to 19 years; ringleader Shabir Ahmed received the longest term.

title: Nine men convicted in Rochdale grooming trial
summary: Nine men were found guilty at Liverpool Crown Court of offences including rape and trafficking girls for sex in Rochdale; it emerged a 2008 complaint had not been prosecuted.

title: Reports say Dutch Catholic institutions castrated boys in the 1950s
summary: Dutch media reported that at least 10 boys in Catholic care were castrated, raising questions about why the 2011 Deetman abuse inquiry omitted the cases.

title: Federal authorities open separate investigation tied to Sandusky and Penn State
summary: The Patriot-News reported that federal prosecutors had subpoenaed records in a separate investigation involving Sandusky, Penn State and The Second Mile.

title: California judge orders Boy Scouts to turn over two decades of confidential abuse files
summary: In a lawsuit over a California troop leader's abuse of a Scout, a judge ordered the Boy Scouts to produce its nationwide 'ineligible volunteer files' from the previous 20 years. Scouting officials disputed that the files had been used to hide abuse.

title: Penn State's insurer asks court to limit its liability for Sandusky claims
summary: Penn State's liability insurer, PMA, asked a Philadelphia court to limit its exposure for abuse claims connected to Sandusky, opening years of coverage litigation.

title: Joe Paterno dies at 85, two months after his firing
summary: Former Penn State coach Joe Paterno died of complications from lung cancer, about ten weeks after trustees removed him amid the Sandusky scandal.

title: Curley and Schultz ordered to stand trial on perjury charges after preliminary hearing
summary: At a preliminary hearing in Harrisburg, McQueary testified and Paterno's grand jury testimony was read into the record; a judge sent the perjury and failure-to-report charges against Curley and Schultz to trial.

title: Sandusky arrested again on charges involving two additional accusers
summary: Sandusky was arrested on new charges after two more alleged victims came forward, bringing the total number of accusers in the criminal case to ten.

title: First civil lawsuit filed against Sandusky, Penn State and The Second Mile
summary: An anonymous plaintiff filed the first civil suit in the scandal, alleging Sandusky abused him and naming Penn State and The Second Mile as defendants.

title: Penn State hires ex-FBI director Louis Freeh to lead internal investigation
summary: Penn State's trustees hired former FBI Director Louis Freeh to conduct an independent investigation of how the university handled allegations against Sandusky.

title: Second Mile president Jack Raykovitz resigns amid Sandusky allegations
summary: Jack Raykovitz resigned as president and CEO of The Second Mile, the youth charity Sandusky founded, after the grand jury report said he had been informed of the 2001 incident.

title: In NBC interview, Sandusky denies abuse but admits showering with boys
summary: In a televised phone interview with NBC's Bob Costas, Sandusky denied being a pedophile while acknowledging he had showered with boys. Prosecutors later used the interview at trial.

title: Penn State puts assistant coach Mike McQueary on paid administrative leave
summary: Penn State placed assistant coach Mike McQueary, who testified he witnessed Sandusky with a boy in a campus shower in 2001, on indefinite paid leave, citing threats against him.

title: U.S. Education Department opens Clery Act review of Penn State
summary: The U.S. Department of Education announced it would investigate whether Penn State violated the Clery Act's campus crime reporting requirements in its handling of the Sandusky allegations.

title: Penn State trustees oust coach Joe Paterno and president Graham Spanier
summary: Penn State's board of trustees removed head football coach Joe Paterno effective immediately, and president Graham Spanier left office, days after the Sandusky charges became public.

title: Curley placed on leave and Schultz steps down as Penn State officials face charges
summary: Penn State said Curley would go on administrative leave and Schultz would step down as the two administrators prepared to answer perjury and failure-to-report charges in court.

title: Jerry Sandusky charged with child sex abuse; Penn State AD Curley and VP Schultz charged
summary: The Pennsylvania attorney general charged Sandusky with sexually abusing eight boys over 15 years. Athletic director Tim Curley and vice president Gary Schultz were charged with perjury and failing to report abuse.

title: Holy See rejects claim it obstructed Irish abuse investigations
summary: In a formal response to the Irish government, the Vatican denied it had interfered with child protection in Cloyne while acknowledging failures.

title: Taoiseach Enda Kenny condemns Vatican over Cloyne findings
summary: In an unprecedented Dáil speech, Kenny accused the Vatican of obstructing an inquiry into abuse and of prioritizing its own reputation.

title: Cloyne Report finds diocese ignored child protection guidelines
institution: Commission of Investigation into the Diocese of Cloyne
summary: The Cloyne inquiry found the diocese failed to report most complaints to police between 1996 and 2009 and said a 1997 Vatican letter had undermined Irish church guidelines.

title: Vatican rejects Karadima appeal and upholds sanctions
summary: The Vatican denied Fernando Karadima's appeal, maintaining its finding that he abused minors and ordering him to a life of prayer and penance.

title: Patriot-News reports grand jury is investigating ex-Penn State coach Jerry Sandusky
summary: The Harrisburg Patriot-News first reported that a state grand jury was investigating allegations that former Penn State defensive coordinator Jerry Sandusky abused a boy. The story went largely unnoticed nationally until charges were filed months later.

title: Times investigation exposes pattern of on-street grooming across northern England
summary: Andrew Norfolk's investigation for The Times identified a pattern of organised grooming of girls in towns across the Midlands and north of England and accused agencies of failing to act.

title: Five Rotherham men jailed for child sex offences
summary: Five men were jailed for sexual offences against girls in Rotherham, an early prosecution in what became a wider exploitation scandal.

title: Belgian court rules church abuse raids illegal
summary: A Brussels court found the June raids unlawful and ordered seized material returned, hampering the investigation.

title: Boy Scouts settle remaining Oregon abuse lawsuits over the same troop leader
summary: Six men who said the same Oregon Scout leader abused them in the 1980s reached undisclosed settlements with the national organization, including the plaintiff in the April verdict. The State of Oregon was due a share of the punitive damages.

title: Vatican indignant over Belgian police raids on church offices
summary: Belgian police seized files from church offices and a cardinal's home in an abuse inquiry, prompting a protest from the Holy See.
