title: Oregon jury orders Boy Scouts to pay $18.5 million in punitive damages in abuse case
summary: Jurors found the Boy Scouts acted with reckless indifference by keeping a leader near Scouts after he had admitted abusing children, and added $18.5 million in punitive damages. The verdict, built on the organization's confidential 'perversion files', was the largest of its kind against the Scouts.

title: Bishop of Bruges resigns after admitting abuse
summary: Bishop Roger Vangheluwe resigned after admitting he had sexually abused a boy years earlier.

title: Oregon jury finds Boy Scouts negligent, awards $1.4 million to former Scout abused by leader
summary: A Portland jury found the Boy Scouts of America failed to protect a Scout from abuse by an assistant Scoutmaster in the early 1980s and awarded $1.4 million in compensatory damages. A separate phase would decide punitive damages, and the Scouts said they would appeal.

title: Guardian examines what Cardinal William Levada knew of 1985 abuse warnings
summary: The Guardian scrutinized the record of Cardinal William Levada, then head of the Vatican's doctrinal office and formerly a U.S. archbishop, regarding early warnings about clergy abuse.

title: Pope Benedict XVI apologizes to Irish abuse victims in pastoral letter
summary: In a letter to Irish Catholics, Benedict XVI expressed shame and remorse to survivors and rebuked Irish bishops for grave errors, while critics said it did not address Vatican responsibility.

title: German priest in abuse case tied to Ratzinger's Munich tenure is suspended
summary: The Munich archdiocese suspended a priest convicted of abuse in 1986 after it emerged he had been returned to pastoral work, a case dating to when the future Benedict XVI led the diocese.

title: Cardinal Brady attended 1975 meetings that swore abuse victims to secrecy
summary: Ireland's primate Cardinal Seán Brady acknowledged he was present as a priest at church inquiries into Fr. Brendan Smyth at which children signed secrecy oaths, but said he would not resign.

title: Jesuit school abuse scandal spreads across Germany
summary: Admissions of past abuse at Berlin's Canisius College opened a wave of revelations at Catholic schools throughout Germany.

title: Second Irish bishop resigns over Murphy Report findings
summary: Another Irish bishop who had served in Dublin announced his resignation after being criticized in the Murphy Report.

title: Murphy Report finds Dublin archdiocese and police covered up child abuse
institution: Commission of Investigation into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin (Murphy Commission)
summary: The Murphy Commission found that successive Dublin archbishops put the church's reputation ahead of children and that police colluded in covering up abuse from 1975 to 2004.

title: Nova Scotia bishop Raymond Lahey wanted on child pornography charges
summary: Police issued a warrant for Bishop Raymond Lahey of Antigonish on charges of possessing and importing child sexual abuse images, days after he resigned.

title: Religious orders refuse to reopen Irish abuse compensation deal
summary: After the Ryan Report, the 18 religious congregations rejected government calls to renegotiate a 2002 indemnity deal that capped their redress contributions.

title: Ryan Report finds abuse endemic in Irish church-run institutions
institution: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse (Ryan Commission)
summary: A nine-year state inquiry concluded that sexual and physical abuse was endemic in industrial schools and reformatories run by Catholic religious orders, and that officials knew.

title: Epstein begins jail sentence after state plea deal tied to federal non-prosecution agreement
summary: Epstein began serving an 18-month sentence after pleading guilty to state prostitution-related charges, under an arrangement with federal prosecutors in Miami that spared him federal charges.

title: Ex-priest Gilbert Gauthe arrested in Texas on sex-offender registration charge
summary: Texas police arrested Gauthe, convicted in 1985, for allegedly failing to give required advance notice before moving under the state's sex-offender registration law.

title: Harvard says it will keep donation from Jeffrey Epstein after his Florida indictment
summary: Harvard said it would not return a large Epstein gift despite the criminal charge he faced in Palm Beach, a decision that later drew scrutiny.

title: Palm Beach police records detail investigation of financier Jeffrey Epstein
summary: Police documents published from the Palm Beach investigation alleged that Epstein paid underage girls for massages at his Florida mansion, following his indictment on a state solicitation charge.

title: Ferns Report finds more than 100 abuse allegations in Irish diocese
summary: The state-appointed Ferns Inquiry found over 100 allegations against 21 priests in the Diocese of Ferns since 1962 and faulted bishops and police for failing to act.

title: Former Temple employee files civil suit accusing Bill Cosby of drugging and assault
summary: Andrea Constand, a former Temple University women's basketball staffer, filed a federal civil lawsuit alleging Cosby drugged and sexually assaulted her at his suburban Philadelphia home in 2004, after prosecutors declined to bring charges. Cosby denied the allegations.

title: Former priest James Porter dies at 70
summary: Porter, whose case helped bring clergy sexual abuse to national attention in 1992 and who pleaded guilty in 1993, died of cancer.

title: Prosecutors seek civil commitment of James Porter as sexually dangerous person
summary: As Porter neared the end of his prison term, Bristol County prosecutors sought to have him civilly committed as a sexually dangerous person.

title: Air Force leaders testify to Senate on Academy sexual assault scandal
summary: Air Force Secretary James Roche and Gen. John Jumper testified before the Senate Armed Services Committee, with Jumper accepting personal responsibility.

title: Panel blames Air Force Academy leaders for years of sexual assaults
summary: An independent panel chaired by Tillie Fowler found leadership failures contributed to 142 reported sexual assaults at the Air Force Academy over a decade and recommended accountability reviews.

title: Boston crisis reopens old wounds in Louisiana, where the scandal first surfaced
summary: As the Boston scandal spread nationally, the Times returned to the Lafayette diocese, where the Gauthe case had first exposed clergy abuse in 1984-85.

title: Globe: Cardinal Law knew of 1985 report on repeat abusers yet reassigned Geoghan
summary: A Spotlight follow-up reported that Cardinal Law had access to the 1985 warnings that abusive priests were likely to reoffend but still assigned Rev. John Geoghan to a parish where he continued to abuse children.

title: Massachusetts bill would extend time for molestation victims to sue
summary: Legislators proposed changing Massachusetts law so that adults abused as children would have more time to bring claims.

title: James Porter denied parole
summary: Massachusetts parole officials denied release to Porter, who was serving his sentence for child sexual abuse.

title: Aberdeen drill sergeant sentenced to 25 years
summary: A military jury sentenced Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson to 25 years for sexually assaulting trainees he supervised at Aberdeen.

title: Newfoundland government makes settlement offers to Mount Cashel claimants
summary: The provincial government offered compensation settlements to former Mount Cashel residents who had sued over abuse suffered in the orphanage.

title: Aberdeen probe widens as sexual misconduct scandal spreads to other bases
summary: Instructors at other training sites faced discipline as the Aberdeen probe prompted a military-wide review and a zero-tolerance order from Defense Secretary William Perry.

title: Army charges trainers at Aberdeen Proving Ground with rape and harassment
summary: The Army charged three trainers at Aberdeen Proving Ground with sexual offenses involving more than a dozen female trainees and sought other possible offenders.

title: Porter victims' lawyer says 20 other area priests face accusations
summary: An attorney for Porter's victims said about 20 other priests in southeastern Massachusetts had also been accused of abuse.

title: James Porter sentenced to 18 to 20 years in prison
summary: A Massachusetts judge sentenced Porter to 18 to 20 years in prison for abusing children in the 1960s.

title: James Porter pleads guilty to assaults committed as a priest
summary: Porter pleaded guilty in Massachusetts to dozens of counts of sexual assault on children committed while he was a priest in the Fall River diocese.

title: Man says aide to Cardinal Law let abuse complaints languish
summary: A man alleged that a top aide to Cardinal Law failed to act on his complaints of clergy abuse, an early sign of problems in Boston's handling of cases.

title: Boston archdiocese adopts sexual misconduct rules for clergy
summary: The Archdiocese of Boston issued formal rules for handling allegations of sexual misconduct by clergy.

title: Ex-priest James Porter goes on trial in Minnesota molestation case
summary: Porter went on trial in Minnesota on charges of molesting a child years after leaving the priesthood, while Massachusetts charges remained pending.

title: 68 Porter accusers reach settlement with Diocese of Fall River
summary: Sixty-eight people who said Porter abused them settled their claims with the Catholic Church in a confidential agreement.

title: U.S. bishops pledge principles for responding to abuse cases
summary: The bishops' conference committed to guidelines for responding to abuse allegations, including prompt investigation and support for victims, though they remained non-binding.

title: U.S. bishops apologize to victims of clergy sexual abuse
summary: Meeting amid the Porter scandal, U.S. Catholic bishops issued an apology to people abused by priests.

title: Boston archdiocese promises abuse policy and review board
summary: The Archdiocese of Boston said it would adopt a formal policy on clergy sexual abuse and create a review board to handle complaints.

title: Report says Porter told the pope of his abuse in the 1960s
summary: The Globe reported that Porter had said he disclosed his abuse of children to the pope in the 1960s before leaving the priesthood, raising questions about what the Vatican knew.

title: Former priest James Porter arrested in Minnesota on Massachusetts abuse charges
summary: Porter was taken into custody in Minnesota on criminal charges brought in Massachusetts over abuse of children in the 1960s.

title: Fall River bishop pledges aid to Porter accusers
summary: The Diocese of Fall River announced it would help pay for counseling and support for people who said Porter abused them.

title: James Porter admits abusing children while a priest and apologizes
summary: Porter publicly acknowledged having abused children during his years as a priest and issued an apology.

title: Navy Secretary Garrett resigns over Tailhook sexual assault scandal
summary: Navy Secretary H. Lawrence Garrett III resigned, accepting responsibility for leadership failures tied to the assaults on women at the 1991 Tailhook convention in Las Vegas.

title: New Fall River bishop Sean O'Malley reaches out to Porter's accusers
summary: Newly appointed Fall River Bishop Sean O'Malley pledged to reach out to people abused by clergy as the Porter case widened.

title: Cardinal Law criticizes press coverage of Porter abuse case
summary: Cardinal Bernard Law publicly faulted news media coverage of the Porter allegations, drawing criticism from accusers and advocates.

title: Massachusetts charitable-immunity law caps church liability at $20,000
summary: The Globe reported that a little-known state law limited damages against charitable organizations such as the church to $20,000 per claim, constraining Porter accusers' potential lawsuits.

title: Dozens more come forward alleging abuse by Fall River priest James Porter
summary: About 30 additional people alleged they were abused by Porter in the 1960s, sharply expanding the case days after the first accounts became public.

title: Nine people allege former priest James Porter abused them, threaten to sue church
summary: Nine adults alleged that James Porter abused them as children while he was a priest in the Diocese of Fall River in the 1960s and said they planned to sue the church.

title: Mount Cashel revelations bring charges of a police and justice cover-up
summary: Testimony and reporting on abuse at the Mount Cashel orphanage raised claims that police and justice officials shelved a 1970s investigation, prompting the Hughes royal commission.

title: Clergy sex abuse scandal shakes Newfoundland
summary: Reports of sexual abuse by Catholic priests in Newfoundland set off a provincial scandal that soon widened to the Christian Brothers' Mount Cashel orphanage.

title: Report: Lafayette diocese has paid about $12 million in Gauthe-related cases, including $1.25M jury award
source: San Jose Mercury News (archived by BishopAccountability.org)
summary: A review of the Gauthe case reported that a 1986 jury awarded one family $1.25 million after the diocese admitted liability, and that the diocese had paid an estimated $12 million across 16 cases.

title: Peterson sends clergy abuse 'Guidelines' package to every U.S. bishop
summary: Rev. Michael Peterson mailed the Doyle-Mouton-Peterson materials to every U.S. diocesan bishop, meaning the hierarchy had a detailed warning about the abuse problem by the end of 1985.

title: Former Louisiana priest Gilbert Gauthe sentenced to 20 years in prison
summary: Under a plea agreement, Gauthe pleaded guilty to charges including child pornography and crimes against nature and received a 20-year prison sentence.

title: Louisiana families sue diocese as priest Gilbert Gauthe faces dozens of molestation counts
summary: Gauthe, who had pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity to 34 counts, was reported to have acknowledged abusing dozens of children, while families pursued suits against the Lafayette diocese, which had already paid $4.2 million to nine families.

title: Doyle, Mouton and Peterson draft confidential manual warning bishops of clergy abuse crisis
summary: Canon lawyer Rev. Thomas Doyle, Gauthe defense attorney F. Ray Mouton and Rev. Michael Peterson wrote a confidential report urging bishops to confront clergy sexual abuse; it was quietly tabled at the bishops' June 1985 meeting.

title: National Catholic Reporter calls clergy abuse cases a pattern of church cover-ups
summary: NCR devoted its front page to clergy sexual abuse cases in Louisiana and several other dioceses, with an editor's note arguing that church structures had failed to act on complaints and an editorial urging diocesan review boards.

title: Times of Acadiana investigation details how Lafayette diocese handled priest Gilbert Gauthe
source: The Times of Acadiana (archived by BishopAccountability.org)
summary: Jason Berry's investigation reported that church leaders in the Diocese of Lafayette received warnings about Rev. Gilbert Gauthe for years before he was removed, and described criminal charges and confidential settlements with families.
